title: Weather Wendy's Forecast
text:
Good morning! This is Weather Wendy with your forecast for Maple Town.

Today will start out sunny and {adjective}. At lunchtime, a light breeze will blow in from the lake. It will smell a little bit like {food}.

This afternoon, look out for a gentle shower of {plural noun}. You may want to carry a {noun} instead of an umbrella. Tonight the clouds will turn {color} and start {verb ending in ing}. Experts say this is normal for a Tuesday.

Tomorrow will be {number} degrees. Please wear sunscreen, a hat, and your most {adjective} sneakers. The wind will blow {adverb} all day, so hold on to your {plural noun}. On Thursday, the moon will be shaped like a {noun}.

This has been Weather Wendy. Remember, if the sky starts to {verb}, just go inside and have a {adjective} snack!

title: Breaking News from Puddle Lane
text:
This is Max Miller with breaking news from Puddle Lane.

At nine o'clock this morning, a small {adjective} cloud floated over Lincoln School and began raining {plural noun}. Students watched {adverb} from the windows.

"I have never seen anything like it," said Principal Gray. "It was very {adjective}. We had to skip recess and {verb} instead."

The cloud then moved to the park, where it rained on a man {verb ending in ing} with his dog. The man said it felt like being tickled by a {noun}. His dog {past tense verb} for an hour.

Weather experts say the cloud is shaped like a {animal} and smells a little like {food}. It is now heading toward the library, where the librarian is holding a {adjective} umbrella. Please keep your windows closed and your {plural noun} indoors.

We will keep you updated. Back to you, {name}!

title: My Weather Journal for Science
text:
Our teacher, Mr. Reed, asked us to write down the weather every day this week. Here is my weather journal.

Monday: Sunny and {adjective}. A cloud shaped like a {noun} floated over my house all day.
Tuesday: Very windy. The wind blew my hat off and carried it {adverb} all the way to the {place}.
Wednesday: Foggy. The fog was so thick that I said good morning to a {noun}.
Thursday: It rained for {number} hours. The puddles were deep enough to {verb} in, so I wore my {adjective} boots.
Friday: A rainbow came out after lunch. It was red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple, and {color}.
Saturday: Cloudy. My dog {past tense verb} at the clouds all morning.

I measured the rain with a cup. On Thursday it filled up with water and three {plural noun}. Mr. Reed says that is very {adjective}.

Next week I will catch a snowflake and keep it in the freezer next to the {plural noun}.

title: Snowman Instructions from a Snow Expert
text:
When it snows, everyone wants to build a snowman. Here is how to make the best one on your street.

Step 1: Put on your boots, your mittens, and your {adjective} scarf.
Step 2: Roll a big ball of snow. Keep rolling until it is as big as a {noun}.
Step 3: Make a middle ball and a small one for the head. Stack them {adverb}.
Step 4: Use two {plural noun} for the eyes and a {noun} for the nose.
Step 5: Add sticks for arms. Some people also give their snowman a {noun} to hold.
Step 6: Give him a hat. Ours wears a {adjective} hat that smells like {food}.
Step 7: Name your snowman. Ours is named {silly word}.

When you are done, stand back and say "{exclamation}!" If your snowman starts to {verb}, you did a great job. Last winter, ours {past tense verb} all the way to the mailbox and back. Then go inside and drink hot cocoa with {plural noun} on top.

title: Windy Day Rules at School
text:
Good morning, students! This is Principal Park. Today will be the windiest day of the year, so please follow these rules.

1. Hold on to your homework {adverb}. Yesterday, the spelling tests blew all the way to the {noun}.
2. Do not fly kites at lunch. Last time, a kite pulled Mr. Bell's {noun} right off the table.
3. If your hair starts to look {adjective}, that is okay. Mine will too.
4. Keep your hats in your backpacks. Three hats are already stuck on the flagpole next to the {plural noun}.
5. If you see a flying {noun}, do not chase it. Tell a teacher, and a teacher will {verb} until it lands.
6. Walk {adverb} near the windows. The wind already borrowed the class hamster's {noun}.

Recess will be indoors. We will play board games, read books about {plural noun}, and do the {animal} dance in the gym. Thank you for {verb ending in ing} so nicely. Have a {adjective} day!

title: A Letter to Mr. Cloud
text:
Dear Mr. Cloud,

My name is Lily. I am seven years old, and I live in the yellow house on Oak Street. You float over my house almost every day at {number} o'clock.

I have a few questions for you. Why are you so {adjective} on Mondays? Do you ever get tired of {verb ending in ing}? My grandpa says clouds eat {plural noun} for breakfast, but I think he is joking. Is it true that you are as soft as a {noun}?

I also have a favor to ask. My birthday party is on Saturday. Could you please rain {plural noun} instead of water? That would be so {adjective}. If you say yes, I will {verb} {adverb} for you and draw you a picture of a {noun}. My dog, {name}, will {verb} for you too.

Your friend on the ground,
Lily

P.S. Please tell the rainbow I like its {color} stripe the best.

title: Grandma Sky's Rainbow Recipe
text:
Have you ever wondered how a rainbow is made? Here is the secret recipe from Grandma Sky's kitchen.

You will need:
1 big cloud
2 cups of sunshine
A bucket of rain
A pinch of glitter
3 {adjective} {plural noun}
A {adjective} spoon

First, put the cloud in a large {noun}. Pour in the rain and stir it {adverb} until it starts to {verb}. Then add the sunshine one cup at a time. Grandma likes to {verb} during this part.

Next, sprinkle in the glitter and a handful of {plural noun}. Grandma Sky says this makes the colors so {adjective}. For an extra stripe, add a little bit of {food}.

Bake the rainbow in the sky for {number} minutes. It should stretch from the school all the way to the {noun}. Serve it after a rainy afternoon, and do not forget to shout "{exclamation}!"

title: Greetings from Breezy Hills
text:
Dear Aunt Rose,

Greetings from Breezy Hills, the windiest town in the country! We are staying here for {number} days.

The wind never stops. This morning it blew my pancakes off my plate and onto a {noun}. Mom had to hold on to her {adjective} sunglasses all through breakfast. Dad's hat is now {verb ending in ing} somewhere over the lake.

Everybody here flies kites. Our neighbor has a kite shaped like a {animal} that is as big as a bus. My kite flew {adverb} and got stuck on a {noun} for an hour.

Yesterday we went to the Wind Museum. They have a jar of wind from long ago. It smells like {plural noun}. The guide told us to {verb} when he opened it. Tomorrow we will watch the Breezy Hills Parade, where everyone goes {verb ending in ing} down Main Street holding a {adjective} {noun}.

Love,
Ben

P.S. I am bringing you a jar of wind. Please open it {adverb}.

title: Dr. Riley's Weather Facts
text:
Hi! I am Dr. Riley, junior weather scientist. Here are my favorite facts.

Fact 1: Snowflakes have six sides. No two look the same, but some look a little like {plural noun}.
Fact 2: Thunder is the sound clouds make when they try to {verb}.
Fact 3: Hail is little balls of ice. In my town, the hail is soft and the size of a {noun}.
Fact 4: Fog is a cloud that got sleepy and decided to {verb} on the ground.
Fact 5: The hottest day in my backyard was {number} degrees. My ice pop melted {adverb} and dripped on my {body part}.
Fact 6: When it rains while the sun is out, a {adjective} rainbow appears. Look closely and you will see a {animal} {verb ending in ing} on it.
Fact 7: Wind is air in a big hurry, usually on its way to the {noun}.

When I grow up, I will wear a {adjective} lab coat and drive a truck full of {plural noun}.

title: The Town Weather Order Form
text:
Thank you for calling the Town Weather Office! To order your weather, fill out this form and drop it in the {adjective} box outside City Hall.

Name: Jada, age 7
Weather needed for: Saturday, my {adjective} soccer game
What kind of sky would you like? Blue, with {number} fluffy clouds. Please make one look like a {noun}.
How warm should it be? Warm enough to {verb} outside, but not so hot that my {food} melts.
Would you like wind? Just a little, so our team flag can wave {adverb}.
Any snow? Not this time. My snow boots are full of {plural noun}.

Anything else? If it has to rain, please make it rain {plural noun}. Coach says that would be very {adjective}. Also, please send a rainbow after the game. My whole team will be {verb ending in ing} on the field.

Thank you! I will pay you with a hug, a {noun}, and two {plural noun}.
